subject: MedSys privacy follow-up: controller/processor scenarios & next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@medsys.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedSys privacy follow-up: controller/processor scenarios & next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on the privacy items you raised: 

1) Controller vs. processor: based on how you described the flow (MedSys sends patient metadata to our hosted inference endpoint; Redwood returns model outputs and we do not persist raw patient PII), we expect the relationship to be: MedSys = Controller, Redwood = Processor. If you want language that explicitly narrows what we process (e.g., allow only tokenized patient IDs and hashed PHI), we can add that to the privacy addendum.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood uses a small set of cloud providers and a managed logging vendor. Standard practice is to list subprocessors in the DPA and provide prior notice for additions. You asked about prior opt-out for any new subprocessor — that is negotiable in the addendum.

3) Breach notification: Redwood's standard DPA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming an incident that affects customer data, with regular status updates. You asked whether 24-hour notice is possible for healthcare customers; we're open to discussing accelerated timelines under a healthcare SLA.

4) Data residency & retention: we can provision a US-only region for your workspace. Default retention for logs is 90 days, but we can extend or shorten retention windows per contract and customer configuration.

5) Logging & access controls: we capture access logs, token-level usage metrics, and role-based access. We can provide an audit log export on request and integrate with your SIEM via SFTP or a secure log delivery option.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to share the current Redwood privacy addendum + DPA template with your contracts team (cc'd) — Ben, attaching the doc we discussed.
- Alicia to confirm whether MedSys needs 24-hr breach notice or standard 72-hr, and whether any subprocessors are deal blockers.
- Marissa to set up a short legal-to-legal sync if needed.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if that helps.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(s) +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (summary: current standard DPA + subprocessor list)

From: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@medsys.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medsys.io
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedSys privacy follow-up: controller/processor scenarios & next steps

Thanks Sofia — helpful summary. Two quick clarifications from legal/security: 

1) Controller/Processor confirmation: can you confirm in writing that Redwood will not act as a co-controller for any decision about the purpose or means of processing patient data? We need an explicit statement for our DPO.

2) Subprocessor notice: MedSys requires notification 30 days prior to onboarding any subprocessor and an ability to object for cause. Is that something Redwood can commit to (we understand exceptions for emergencies, but need baseline 30 days)?

3) Breach chronology: 72 hours is acceptable as a starting point, but we need a commitment to daily status updates until remediation is complete. Also: will Redwood provide timeline and root cause analysis within 30 days?

4) Data residency: confirmed — US-only residency is mandatory. Can you provide the US region and whether backups cross regions?

5) Retention: can you provide a simple matrix (data type -> default retention -> configurable max/min)? Our compliance team prefers concrete numbers.

If you can share the addendum and DPA with redlines, we'll review and route to contracts. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal next week.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Nguyen
Senior Privacy Counsel, MedSys Health

--

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 18:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedSys privacy follow-up: controller/processor scenarios & next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks for the detailed list of asks, really helpful. Short answers inline below; I'll follow up with the legal team for formal language.

1) Co-controller: Redwood's standard position is processor-only. We will provide a one-line statement in the addendum that Redwood does not make decisions about the purpose or means of processing customer data unless otherwise agreed in writing.

2) 30-day subprocessor notice: we provide notification of new subprocessors and a 30-day review window in our enterprise DPA. For critical concerns you may raise an objection and request mitigation (e.g., contractual flow-down or alternative vendor). Emergency additions can be handled with immediate notice and a post-facto review.

3) Breach timelines: confirm 72-hour initial notification, daily status updates until resolved, and a root cause and remediation plan within 30 days. We can include this in the SLA appendix for healthcare customers.

4) Residency & backups: US-only workspace will be provisioned in the us-west-2 region (AWS). Backups are stored within the same region by default; cross-region replication is optional and must be disabled for MedSys.

5) Retention matrix: see quick matrix below (we will provide a formal table in the DPA):
- Inference inputs (raw): default 7 days, configurable 0–90 days
- Inference outputs (model responses): default 30 days, configurable 0–365 days
- Audit logs/access logs: default 90 days, configurable 30–730 days

Action items: Ben will send the DPA and the privacy-addendum doc for your contracts team. If you confirm 30-day subprocessors and the 72-hour/30-day breach cadence, we'll proceed to legal redlines.

Best,
Sofia
